cost_basis: EXTRAPOLATED, DERIVED, NOT MEASURED -- and the box cannot read its own billing (COMPUTE_BUDGET_CHARTER sec.5), so every dollar figure here is DERIVED at the owner-stated rate and NEVER measured. THERE IS NO MEASURED VMFL006 COST: the pre-freeze smoke's COST.txt records total_wall_s=0 and total_core_min=0.0 (endTime 20 completed in under one integer second, unresolved), so it anchors nothing. The estimate is EXTRAPOLATED from cell counts: (4000+16000+64000) cells x 3000 iterations = 2.52e8 cell-steps, at an ASSUMED single-core throughput of 5e5 to 5e6 cell-steps/s/core for a steadyState scalar-transport solve (one T equation per iteration, smoothSolver/symGaussSeidel nSweeps 2 relTol 0.01, small laminar mesh). That gives a BRACKET of 0.84 core-min (fast) to 8.4 core-min (slow) for the whole three-level run; cost_core_min_estimate=4.6 is the bracket midpoint, NOT a measurement, and the full bracket is what the ESTIMATE_OVERRUN watcher should read this figure against. THE CAP CAP_CORE_MIN=18 IS UNCHANGED; the launcher's per-level timeout fires only if throughput falls below 2.33e5 cell-steps/s (about 2.4x worse than the pessimistic assumption). THE ESTIMATE-VERSUS-ACTUAL CALIBRATION ROW IN docs/COST_CALIBRATION.md IS OWED AT COMPLETION (rule 12, Sanaa 2026-08-23), and this 4.6 midpoint with its 0.8-8.4 bracket is what the actual will be compared against.
memory_floor_basis: 1.0 GB is DERIVED FROM THE CASE SIZE AND IS NOT MEASURED. The family is a 2D axisymmetric 5deg wedge at 4000 / 16000 / 64000 cells running scalarTransportFoam SERIAL (ranks 1); the momentum equation is not solved (the parabola is imposed). A single scalar field on at most 64000 cells is of order a few MB; a gigabyte is generous by orders of magnitude and is stated as a scheduling floor, not a profiled footprint. It is an INFRASTRUCTURE field: a wrong value here is a bookkeeping defect that can misschedule the run and can NEVER produce NOT A RESULT (L-342).
